name: HER2-low and HER2-ultralow
summary: HER2-low (IHC 1+, or IHC 2+ without ISH amplification) and HER2-ultralow (faint, incomplete membrane staining in a minority of cells, IHC >0 but <1+) are therapeutically defined categories within traditionally HER2-negative breast cancer, introduced because of trastuzumab deruxtecan activity.
biology: HER2-low is not considered a distinct biological subtype; it reflects low-level HER2 protein expression without gene amplification, and its frequency is higher in hormone receptor-positive than triple-negative disease. The activity of trastuzumab deruxtecan in this population relates to efficient payload delivery and a membrane-permeable topoisomerase I inhibitor payload producing a bystander effect, rather than dependence on HER2 signalling.

methods: Immunohistochemistry with ASCO/CAP scoring, with careful attention to the low end of the scale
In situ hybridisation for IHC 2+ cases
testing.notes: Interobserver variability is considerable between IHC 0, ultralow and 1+. Expression is heterogeneous between primary and metastatic sites and over time, so re-testing of archival or new samples may change eligibility. Assays were not originally designed to discriminate low-level expression.

predictiveRelevance: HER2-low and HER2-ultralow status identifies patients with metastatic breast cancer eligible for trastuzumab deruxtecan after prior therapy (and, for hormone receptor-positive disease, after endocrine-based therapy). It is not an indication for traditional HER2-targeted antibodies or TKIs, which lack meaningful activity in this population.
resistance: Downregulation of HER2 expression and ADC internalisation
Payload resistance (e.g. topoisomerase I alterations, drug efflux)
Cross-resistance between sequential topoisomerase I inhibitor-payload ADCs is an area of active study
